events.text: The Concord is trying to hold Meridian. There are evacuation lists on every wall, a docking queue that does not move, and a Director who has stopped sleeping. 'We have the guns and the berths,' she says, 'and we do not have the fuel to keep the lanes open or the plate to keep the walls up. Five thousand credits would buy both. The Authority will not fund it. The Authority will be late.' She looks at your ship, and at the queue behind you. 'Nobody has ever held a station against the tide. I would like to see how it is done.'

outcomes.text: You sign the defence order. The Director stamps it twice, once for each of you, and for the first time in weeks the queue starts to move. By the end of the week the walls have your name chalked on the inside.

choices.text: Ask to see the lines first.

outcomes.text: She walks you up through the evacuation decks and out onto the long wall, where volunteers in borrowed suits are bolting plate over plate. Beyond the wall the dark has a faint green edge.

choices.text: Not yet. The tide is still coming.

outcomes.text: 'It always is,' says the Director, and stamps something that has nothing to do with you.

events.text: The wall is a hundred metres of mismatched plate with a catwalk along the top. There is a hook by the hatch at helmet height, and a kettle on a ledge, and a note chalked beside it: DON'T GET USED TO IT. A volunteer sees you looking and waves a welding mask. Down the length of the wall, one by one, the lamps come on.

choices.text: Stay and fund the line. (5,000 credits)

outcomes.text: You hang your helmet on the hook. It fits. Behind you the Director says nothing, loudly, for a long time, and then 'Tea?'
'Take your time,' says the Director. 'The wall is not going anywhere. Neither is the number five thousand.'
